stop_condition: Every acceptance criterion in the SPEC is settled by evidence, and every shipped surface this candidate changed or falsified has been checked for a FALSE claim; findings that only sharpen a true claim are classified v5.0.1 rather than re-reviewed.

findings.evidence: BLOCKING. The comment justifying the runner-wide stub reads, in the present tense: "`true` is chosen over an empty value deliberately: the upgrade arm treats a failed command as \"continuing on the current bd\", which is the behaviour a spec wants, while an empty command would make the arm's own guard the thing under test." FALSE at a6a8d39. The round-5 fix is exactly the removal of that behaviour: `git diff 1ea00bb a6a8d39 -- install.sh` shows `-        return 0` replaced by `+        refuse_below_floor "$current" opt-in` at install.sh:753-757 (failed command) and the new below-floor check at :767-776. MEASURED, host bd hashed before and after (86e81a32... unchanged throughout): with a fake bd reporting 0.47.1 on PATH, `env PATH=<fake> BD_UPGRADE_COMMAND=false CWP_BEADS_UPGRADE=1 bash install.sh <target>` exits rc=1, prints "REFUSING to install", `grep -c 'Continuing on bd'` = 0, and `find <target> -type f | wc -l` = 0. The literal value the comment defends, `BD_UPGRADE_COMMAND=true`, behaves the same way: rc=1, "REFUSING to install", 0 files. NOTHING continues on the current bd. THE CANDIDATE CONTRADICTS ITSELF MECHANICALLY, IN THE SAME COMMIT: installer-flags 9.13 asserts "...and it does not claim to be continuing" against `contains "$OPTF_OUT" "Continuing on bd"` (PASS; whole spec rc=0, PASSED: 133 assertions), and installer-beads-upgrade 5.3/5.4 assert "the install is REFUSED, exit 1, not continued on 0.47.1" and "nothing says it is continuing" (PASS; BD_SHIM_ONLY=1 L2 run, rc=0, pass=62 fail=0). PROVENANCE: new text in this change set -- `git diff 32b12b2 a6a8d39 -- .claude/scripts/tests/run-tests.sh` shows the whole block as `+` lines. It is present tense while the SAME block uses past tense deliberately where it means the past ("which until 2026-10-02 defaulted to", "did exactly that", "install.sh no longer has an auto-upgrade default"), so the tense is a choice, not a slip. NO SELF-CORRECTION anywhere in the block -- the surrounding lines are about the canary and the curl -- which is the exact discriminator round 5 used to separate R5-F2 (blocking) from R5-F5 (v5.0.1).
findings.description: The runner's rationale for exporting BD_UPGRADE_COMMAND=true states, as current behaviour, the precise thing this candidate's headline change removed: that a failed upgrade command lets the install continue on the old bd. It now refuses with exit 1. The stub value remains correct and more important than ever; the reason given for it is false, and it is the one behavioural fact a maintainer most needs right about this release.

findings.evidence: BLOCKING. The comment on the hard floor reads: "HARD FLOOR. Deliberately still 0.47: every bd call the plugin makes is version-tolerant (the `--include-comments || plain` read chains), so an older bd is degraded, not broken, and refusing the install outright would strand users rather than help them. RECOMMENDED_BD_VERSION below is how they move." At a6a8d39 the installer refuses the install outright for every bd in [0.47, 1.1.2) -- MEASURED on four independent paths with a fake bd 0.47.1, all rc=1 with no .claude/ and 0 files written: --skip-beads-upgrade (+CWP_BEADS_UPGRADE=1), CWP_SKIP_BEADS_UPGRADE=1, opt-in with BD_UPGRADE_COMMAND=false, opt-in with BD_UPGRADE_COMMAND=true; control at the floor installs (rc=0, .claude present, 168 files). So "refusing the install outright would strand users rather than help them" is offered as the live reason for a policy the shipped code reverses, four lines above RECOMMENDED_BD_VERSION itself, and "RECOMMENDED_BD_VERSION below is how they move" describes a soft offer where a hard refusal now stands. DECISIVE, AND INTERNAL TO THE CANDIDATE: install.ps1's twin of this exact block was REWRITTEN in this same commit to the correct wording -- install.ps1:108-111, "CLI FLOOR. Deliberately still 0.47, matching install.sh (packaging-parity pins both). It is checked first and only rejects a bd too old to talk to; it does not admit one. Anything below $RecommendedBdVersion is then REFUSED by Invoke-BeadsUpgradeIfOld, with the upgrade procedure." The PowerShell copy was fixed; the bash original was not. PROVENANCE: `git blame -L 69,77 a6a8d39 -- install.sh` attributes lines 70-73 to fdfd6ce7 (2026-08-03) and `git diff 32b12b2 a6a8d39 -- install.sh` touches none of them -- untouched context, the SAME origin commit and the SAME reasoning round 5 applied to R5-F3: the candidate did not write the sentence but did falsify it. Corroborating that this is the last survivor of a sweep that was otherwise completed: `git grep -i 'hard floor is 0.47' a6a8d39` returns NOTHING (the R5-F1 round removed that phrase from install.sh --help and from install.ps1), and `git grep -i 'degraded, not broken' a6a8d39` returns exactly one hit -- this one.
findings.description: install.sh's own hard-floor comment still states the retired advisory policy as the live reason the installer does not refuse an old bd outright, while install.sh now does exactly that. The PowerShell twin of the same paragraph was corrected in this commit, which is what makes the bash copy an incomplete edit rather than a judgement call.

findings.location: install.ps1:461-462 (inside Invoke-RefuseBelowFloor's SCOPE OF THIS CLAIM block)
findings.evidence: BLOCKING, and the finding is the SECOND clause only. The block reads: "...install.ps1 has never been executed anywhere, on any machine or in CI; the Windows job stages a bd shim and exercises the installer's argument surface, not this path." THE FIRST CLAUSE IS TRUE and independently corroborated -- docs/RELEASE_AUDIT.md rows R25 and S6 record "install.ps1 has never run on a Windows runner" and name the binding obstacle (gh token scopes lack `workflow`), and README:353-357 says the job "is committed but has not been dispatched". THE SECOND CLAUSE IS FALSE ON BOTH HALVES. (a) `.github/workflows/windows-install.yml` is not an argument-surface probe: line 140 runs `& "$env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE/install.ps1" -Path $target -Mode 1` end to end, then asserts the rendered install across 27 parity rows and runs the target's own workflow-doctor.sh; its own header lines 1-2 say "executes install.ps1 for real on windows-latest and asserts the rendered install matches the parity spec." (b) "not this path" is the inverse of the truth at a6a8d39. The job's shim prints `bd version 0.47.0` (windows-install.yml:95), sized at lines 84-85 to "a version >= the installer's MinBdVersion (0.47)". 0.47.0 is below $RecommendedBdVersion 1.1.2, so the call at install.ps1:644 enters Invoke-BeadsUpgradeIfOld; $BdUpgradeCommand defaults to "" (install.ps1:130), so the guard at :524 (`$SkipBeadsUpgrade -or (-not $BdUpgradeCommand) -or ($env:CWP_BEADS_UPGRADE -ne "1")`) fires and calls Invoke-RefuseBelowFloor, which exits 1 at :498. A dispatch lands on EXACTLY this path, as the first thing the installer does. PROVENANCE: new text in this change set -- `git diff 32b12b2 a6a8d39 -- install.ps1 | grep 'argument surface'` returns a `+` line. windows-install.yml is NOT in the 23-file change set (`git diff --name-only 32b12b2 a6a8d39 | grep -c windows-install` = 0), so it is untouched context the candidate falsified. SCOPE NOTE, since the comment is about verification strength: pwsh is not on this host (`command -v pwsh` -> absent), so I could not reproduce the commit message's "parses with 0 errors under pwsh 7.4.6" claim; this finding rests on reading install.ps1 and windows-install.yml, which is the same standard the file itself asks to be held to.
findings.description: A new comment in install.ps1 reaches the right conclusion (never executed) via a checkable and false premise about what the committed Windows job does. The job executes the installer end to end, and its 0.47.0 shim now drives it straight into the very refusal path the comment says it does not reach -- which is also what the false premise conceals (see R6-F4).

findings.evidence: v5.0.1. Not itself a false claim -- the consequence R6-F3's wrong premise hides. With the shim at `bd version 0.47.0`, install.ps1 at a6a8d39 exits 1 having written nothing, so the row at :190, `Add-Result "install.ps1 did not abort (exit 0 = self-verified, 3 = see doctor step)" (($installRc -eq 0) -or ($installRc -eq 3))`, fails, and every rendered-tree assertion after it fails with it. The repo's only Windows evidence artifact -- the one README:353-357 and docs/RELEASE_AUDIT.md R25/R26/S6/Q7/I5 all name as the flip-path from PROVEN-WITH-CAVEAT to PROVEN -- cannot pass at this SHA without its shim being raised. The candidate migrated the three bash fixtures with the same defect IN THIS COMMIT: installer-manifest-parity.sh, installer-target-functional.sh and installer-v3-upgrade.sh each stopped hardcoding `0.99.0` and now read RECOMMENDED_BD_VERSION out of install.sh, with a harness-error guard if the read fails. The Windows shim is the one fixture of the four that was not migrated. Classified v5.0.1 rather than blocking because the job is workflow_dispatch-only and undispatched, and because README does not claim it passes -- only that it exists. UNVERIFIED SUGGESTION -- verify before adoption: raise the shim to report $RecommendedBdVersion, derived from install.ps1 the way the three bash fakes derive it from install.sh rather than hardcoded, so the next floor move does not silently re-break it.
findings.description: The v5 bd floor makes the committed windows-install.yml job unpassable: its bd shim reports 0.47.0, which install.ps1 now refuses before writing anything. Three sibling bash fixtures with the identical defect were fixed in this same commit; this one was missed.

findings.location: README.md:299-300 and CHANGELOG.md:174-175 ("REFUSES before writing anything")
findings.evidence: v5.0.1, and it is a STRONGER instance than the one already filed. Round 5's R5-F6 (filed as tg72) named only `mkdir -p "$TARGET"` at install.sh:454. MEASURED, both paths, at a6a8d39. (1) mkdir: a target path that does not exist is CREATED and then the installer refuses -- probe: target absent before, `rc=1`, directory present after. (2) NEW: on the opt-in path the target's `.beads/issues.jsonl` is REWRITTEN before the refusal. Probe with a fake bd 0.47.1 whose `sync --flush-only` actually rewrites the ledger (as the real one does), `BD_UPGRADE_COMMAND=false CWP_BEADS_UPGRADE=1`: rc=1, `.claude` absent, and the ledger went from `{"id":"ORIGINAL-LEDGER","comments":[{"t":"a"}]}` to `{"id":"REWRITTEN-BY-FLUSH","comments":[{"t":"a"}]}`. The `.pre-upgrade.bak` copy is also written and then removed at install.sh:748 before the Step 2 refusal. HARM IS LOW and the candidate is honest at the point of use: the operator must deliberately set two variables to reach it, the write is a flush performed by their OWN bd (step 1 of the procedure the installer prints), and install.sh's refusal text distinguishes correctly -- "No plugin file has been written" on the opt-in arm versus "Nothing has been written" otherwise (both observed). refuse_below_floor's own header at install.sh:560-566 discloses the re-flush explicitly, which is why the header is NOT a finding. Only the two release surfaces overreach. Classified v5.0.1 to stay consistent with round 5's LOW on the same sentence and the operator's filing of tg72, but tg72 as filed names only the mkdir and so understates its own scope.
findings.description: The unqualified "REFUSES before writing anything" on both release surfaces is false on two paths, not one: the already-filed mkdir, and a ledger rewrite inside the target's .beads/ on the opt-in path. The installer's own printed wording and refuse_below_floor's header are already accurate; tg72 should be widened to cover the second path.

findings.evidence: v5.0.1. Both floors are gated on a parseable version: `[ -n "$BD_VERSION_NUM" ]` at :501 guards the MIN_BD_VERSION check, and `[ -n "$current" ] || return 0` at :633 is the first line of upgrade_beads_if_old. Both are untouched context (neither appears as a changed line in `git diff 32b12b2 a6a8d39 -- install.sh`). MEASURED: a fake bd printing `bd version unknown-dev` (no dotted-numeric for the `grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?'` at :497 to find) installs cleanly -- rc=0, `grep -c 'REFUSING to install'` = 0, 168 files written with --skip-mcp-deps --skip-verify, and the installer reports "OK Beads installed (bd version unknown-dev)". NOT classified blocking: the new enforcement claim at install.sh:535-540 is scoped to "Every path through upgrade_beads_if_old that would leave bd below RECOMMENDED_BD_VERSION", and an unreadable version is not KNOWN to be below, so the sentence is not literally falsified; and no real beads release prints an unparseable version. But README:366's "Supported range: >= 1.1.2, the floor the installer enforces" and CHANGELOG:171's "bd must be 1.1.2 or newer BEFORE you run the installer" are the strongest version of the claim yet shipped, and this is the hole directly under them. UNVERIFIED SUGGESTION -- verify before adoption: treat an unparseable `bd --version` as a refusal with its own message rather than as a silent pass, so "cannot read your bd's version" and "your bd is supported" stop rendering identically.
findings.description: A bd whose --version carries no dotted-numeric bypasses both the hard floor and the recommended floor and installs cleanly. Pre-existing and degenerate, but it sits directly under the newly strengthened "the floor the installer enforces" claim.

findings.location: commit message of a6a8d39, MEASURED section
findings.evidence: v5.0.1. The section says "On this tree, on the macOS host: ... L1, after that check was corrected: packaging-parity 658 PASSED, run-tests rc=0", and four bullets later "At the time of this commit, a full L1 tier on this exact tree had NOT yet run." run-tests.sh IS the L1 tier and its rc=0 requires the EXPECTED_SPECS completeness floor to hold, so the two sentences are in tension as written. The intended scoping is recoverable from the next clause of the same sentence -- "It runs next, in the same container", referring back to the linux/arm64 CI-matched container of the first bullet -- and the bullet then names the remaining gaps honestly ("CI had not run this SHA either, and the container is arm64 where CI is amd64"). A reader of the whole bullet reaches the true statement, which is the same discriminator round 5 used to keep R5-F5 non-blocking. EVERY FIGURE IN THAT SECTION THAT I COULD RUN UNDER THE QUIESCENCE CONSTRAINT WAS REPRODUCED AT a6a8d39, each with its rc: packaging-parity PASSED 658 (rc=0), installer-flags PASSED 133 (rc=0), workflow-doctor PASSED 230 (rc=0), workflow-manifest PASSED 230 (rc=0), verify-release-manifest PASSED 83 (rc=0), release-claims-check PASSED 29 (rc=0), approval-record-disclosure-claim 238 passed 0 failed (rc=0), L2 installer-beads-upgrade pass=62 fail=0 (rc=0), make lint rc=0. The free-mutant claim for packaging-parity is consistent by construction: all four pinned strings ("Upgrade by hand: ", refuse_below_floor / Invoke-RefuseBelowFloor, "does not admit a bd below", "still below") are absent at 1ea00bb in BOTH installers and present at a6a8d39, which is exactly the 8 parity_both legs of 8.16 and 8.20-8.22. UNVERIFIED SUGGESTION -- verify before adoption: "a full L1 tier on this exact tree had not yet run IN THE CI-MATCHED CONTAINER."
findings.description: The MEASURED section reports run-tests rc=0 on this tree and then says no full L1 tier had run on this tree. The qualifier "in the same container" is present but arrives after the unqualified sentence. Every figure I could reproduce under quiescence matched.

findings.evidence: v5.0.1. "Its lane did NOT measure it until 2026-10-02" presupposes that the l1-unit lane measures 1.1.2:53 after that date. README:388-389, shipped in the same commit, declines to claim that: "CI floor coverage UNCONFIRMED ... this row will not claim otherwise until the lane is shown to measure 1.1.2." The evidence the doctor comment then offers is a CONTAINER, not CI, and it says so three lines later ("a full L1 tier in a container matched to CI on run user, locale, dolt and bd version measured 1.1.2:53 from /usr/local/bin/bd and passed, rc=0, 76/76 -- on linux/arm64, where CI is amd64"), so the paragraph self-corrects. What it does not say, and the commit message does, is WHICH tree that run was on: b870d030, which the commit message states is "before the round-5 fixes". The three fixes the sentence credits ("With them in place") were in place at b870d030, so the claim is true as scoped; naming the tree would close the gap. UNVERIFIED SUGGESTION -- verify before adoption: "Its lane had not been SHOWN to measure it as of 2026-10-02", plus the tree the container run was on.
findings.description: The doctor's floor-row narrative implies post-2026-10-02 CI measurement of 1.1.2:53 that README explicitly refuses to claim, and the container run it cites is not identified by tree. It self-corrects within the paragraph, so this is precision, not a false claim.
